ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A certain amount of ideal gas is confined in a cylinder by a piston, and a partition divides the gas into two parts, A and B. Initially, the volumes of A and B are both $V$, and their pressures are both equal to the atmospheric pressure $p_{0}$. The partition is equipped with a pressure sensor and a control device. The partition will slide when the pressure difference between the two sides exceeds $0.5p_{0}$, otherwise the partition will remain stationary. The temperature of the gas is kept constant throughout the process. The piston is slowly pushed to the right, reducing the volume of B to $\frac{V}{2}$.

1. Determine the pressure of B.
2. Determine the volume of A.
3. Then the piston is slowly moved back to its initial position to the left. Determine the volume of A and the pressure of B at this time.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a horizontal cylinder, with a diagonally shaded piston on the left side, and a vertical partition/baffle (Baffle) in the middle of the cylinder. The partition divides the gas into two parts: the part between the piston and the partition is labeled A, and the part from the right side of the partition to the rounded closed end of the cylinder is labeled B. Reasoning: In the initial state, both parts of the gas satisfy V_A=V_B=V, p_A=p_B=p_0, and the whole process is isothermal, so the amounts of substance of the gases on the two sides do not change, and respectively have the isothermal relations p_A V_A=p_0V, p_B V_B=p_0V. When the piston is slowly pushed to the right, A is first compressed and the partition does not move, until the pressure difference between the two sides reaches the control threshold. Then the partition slides, and in the quasi-static process maintains the limiting pressure difference p_A-p_B=0.5p_0. The problem statement gives that the volume of B at the endpoint is V_B=V/2, therefore from p_BV_B=p_0V, p_B=2p_0 is obtained. At this time it is still in the sliding limiting state, so p_A=p_B+0.5p_0=2.5p_0. Thus the volume of A is V_A=p_0V/p_A=p_0V/(2.5p_0)=0.4V. Next the piston slowly returns leftward to the initial position. Starting from the above endpoint, at first the partition does not move, A expands, p_A decreases, while B keeps V_B=V/2, p_B=2p_0, until the pressure difference reversely reaches p_B-p_A=0.5p_0. After that the partition slides leftward and maintains p_B-p_A=0.5p_0. When the piston returns to the initial position, the total gas volume in the cylinder is restored to 2V, so let at this time V_A'=x, V_B'=2V-x. From the isothermal relations p_A'=p_0V/x, p_B'=p_0V/(2V-x), and satisfying p_B'-p_A'=0.5p_0, namely V/(2V-x)-V/x=1/2. Let X=x/V, then 1/(2-X)-1/X=1/2, solving gives X=\sqrt{5}-1 (discard the negative root). Therefore V_A'=(\sqrt{5}-1)V. At this time V_B'=(3-\sqrt{5})V, so p_B'=p_0V/V_B'=p_0/(3-\sqrt{5})=((3+\sqrt{5})/4)p_0.
